name: Yellow socialism
summary: Yellow socialism was a French workers' movement founded by Pierre Biétry in 1902 as a rival to Marxist red socialism. It rejected class struggle, the general strike and state collectivism, and wanted workers to gain property and a share of profits through trade syndicates cooperating with employers under a strong national state. It was patriotic, hostile to internationalism and immigration, and increasingly antisemitic.
scope: The Fédération nationale des Jaunes de France (1902-c.1912) around Pierre Biétry, based mainly on the federation's program and speeches in Biétry's Le socialisme et les Jaunes (1906). It excludes the later Marxist use of 'yellow' as an insult for any non-Marxist or social-democratic socialism, and American business unionism.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The 1904 program backs mutual aid, assistance and workers' pensions but names no health system; a state-guaranteed minimum fits a strong-state corporatism only by inference.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The Jaunes wanted wages and hours fixed by joint employer-worker syndicates, not by statute, and also wanted workers' conditions improved; a legal wage floor is not addressed.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Biétry attacked state collectivism but also the anarchy of the wage system; he wanted organised cooperation between capital and labour rather than either pure market or state.

public-ownership.rationale: The program's point 5 fights municipal and state collectivism, which turns workers into functionaries under an anonymous master harsher than the employer.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: No tax program appears in the Jaunes texts; they opposed attacks on property but wanted workers to rise, so adherents have no clear line on taxing the rich.

unions-good.rationale: The Jaunes built and promoted their own syndicates, mixed with employers, while fighting the CGT and independent class unions, so they endorse unions only of their own kind.

property-fundamental.rationale: The program lists the right of property first and demands property rights without restriction for syndicates; Biétry called himself the defender of propriété against collectivism.

regulate-corporations.rationale: They wanted capital and labour tied together by profit sharing, not employers constrained by the state; they distrusted state intervention yet criticised anonymous capital, so no clear stance.

cut-welfare.rationale: The program wants mutual aid, assistance and pensions for workers and charity encouraged, so a committed Jaune does not accept cutting welfare as such, though it prefers private and mutual forms.

worker-ownership.rationale: Jaunes wanted workers to buy shares in their firms so that wage labour moves toward individual ownership; this is shareholding, not collective ownership of the whole business.

surveillance-ok.rationale: The movement sat under a strong authoritarian state and was nationalist and anti-revolutionary, so security measures against subversion would be accepted; no text addresses terrorism.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Anachronistic; a conservative, nationalist moralist movement of 1900 would not favour legalising recreational drugs.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Biétry's own press was openly antisemitic and polemical, so adherents would not favour limits on it; the issue is anachronistic.

strong-leader.rationale: Sources say the system was to sit under a strong authoritarian state and Biétry attacked the gridlocked parliament, from which support for a strong leader is inferred; Biétry himself served as an elected deputy.

state-harmful.rationale: Biétry saw the state as needed to arbitrate and to protect national unity, and the movement is described as resting on a strong state, so abolishing it is out.

limit-guns.rationale: No source addresses firearms; the movement's emphasis on order and patriotism cuts both ways.

empower-police-military.rationale: The Jaunes were patriotic and anti-revolutionary and stressed national strength, so they would favour a stronger army and order.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Anachronistic; a morally conservative movement defending the family would oppose it.

decide-locally.rationale: Biétry stressed associations built up by trade and region, but within a strong national state; a clear preference for local over national decision is not stated.

rehabilitation.rationale: No penal doctrine is documented; a law-and-order nationalist movement leans to punishment but the Jaunes also stressed education.

traditional-family.rationale: The conclusion places individual, family, province and fatherland on association, and a women's league supported the Jaunes, which fits a family-centred conservatism.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Anachronistic; a conservative, nationalist movement of 1900-1910 would be firmly against it.

abortion-legal.rationale: Anachronistic; the movement's pro-family, pro-nation stance points against legal abortion.

more-religion-public.rationale: Biétry opposed anticlericalism in schools and honoured liberty of conscience as absolute, yet did not ask for a state religion, so adherents are neutral.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Anachronistic; given the movement's nationalism and antisemitism, it would reject programmes of redress for racial groups.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Anachronistic; a conservative movement of this period assumed natural sex roles.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Biétry held that the worker must be tied to the fatherland by property and that internationalism destroys national unity; national preservation is central.

gradual-change.rationale: The Jaunes rejected revolution and the general strike and wanted gradual social uplift through property and joint agreements.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Yellow socialists opposed immigration as a threat to native-born workers' wages and jobs; Biétry cited foreign workers in Paris against the internationalist worker.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The movement attacked internationalism as a trap for French workers and sovereign nation as the frame; supranational power is contrary to its core.

free-trade.rationale: No tariff programme in the Jaunes texts, but a nationalist movement worried about foreign workers would doubt unrestricted trade; Biétry did lament industries unable to export.

nation-first.rationale: Biétry's speeches say workers' interests are bound to the grandeur and strength of the fatherland and call internationalism a mistake.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Not addressed; a national-interest movement would probably not back foreign interventions for human rights.

open-borders.rationale: The Jaunes opposed immigration as a threat to native wages and defended national unity against internationalism.

limit-growth.rationale: Anachronistic; an industrial-era movement that wanted workers to share in industrial profits would not limit growth.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic; no basis in sources for an answer, and no obvious principle decides it.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Anachronistic; Biétry did not rely on technology but on social association, though he defended the industrial apparatus of civilisation.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Anachronistic and unaddressed; industrial-nationalist leanings are offset by no stated view.

revolution-justified.rationale: The program rejects collectivist revolution and Biétry turned against Marxism and the general strike; workers should enter the factory as partners, not burn it.

experts-over-public.rationale: Biétry proposed chambers of competence to vet economic laws, which gives experts a role, but he also appealed to workers directly.

central-planning.rationale: The movement fought collectivism and state control of the economy as dangerous to workers.

socialized-markets.rationale: Markets with worker or public owners is not Jaune doctrine; they wanted individual worker ownership of shares inside private firms.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not addressed anywhere in the Jaunes documents I read.

tax-inheritance.rationale: The movement defended property rights for all and wanted workers to accumulate property, so heavy inheritance tax would conflict, though they did not discuss it.

basic-income.rationale: Anachronistic; the Jaunes wanted workers to earn property and independence through association and not unconditional state payments.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Not stated directly; a nationalist, anti-foreign-labour movement inclined to protect national work, though Biétry also lamented industries unable to export.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The movement opposed state collectivism and wanted workers and employers to arrange matters through joint syndicates.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The program demands accession of labour to capital and property, and Biétry's propriétarisme aims to spread ownership to more people.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Biétry wanted to transform wage labour toward individual ownership and profit sharing, not abolish money or wages.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not addressed; a statist-nationalist order would hardly want central banks left to the market.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: The 1904 programme has employers' and workers' syndicates agree hours by trade and region, a corporatist idea, but it does not make them state-recognised bodies or give them a role in setting prices.

one-party-rule.rationale: The federation aimed to form a Party of National Interests but Biétry sat in a plural parliament; a single ruling party is not documented.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Biétry was a republican radical turned nationalist who spoke as a deputy of the republic; monarchy is not his programme, though the movement mixed with the right.

democracy-best.rationale: Biétry criticised an omnipotent parliament while sitting in it and sources describe a strong authoritarian state; adherents are split on democracy as supreme.

direct-votes.rationale: He wanted representative bodies corrected by chambers of competence, not direct votes on laws.

workers-councils.rationale: The Jaunes rejected socialist revolution and class rule and wanted cooperation with employers in a national framework.

right-to-secede.rationale: National unity under the tricolour is a central theme of Biétry's speeches.

natural-rulers.rationale: No documented view; the movement appealed to workers yet endorsed a strong state.

political-violence-never.rationale: The movement rejected revolutionary violence yet was belligerently nationalist; no clear pacifist principle.

war-builds-character.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; patriotism is central but no doctrine of war's value.

separate-church-state.rationale: Biétry opposed anticlericalism, especially in schools, and filed a bill to separate schools from the state, which is not the same as church-state separation; leans against strict separation.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The program demands absolute liberty of conscience and Biétry said Jaunes need not destroy any religion; scriptural law is not part of it.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The movement relied on a strong state and a national army, and valued patriotism.

military-superiority.rationale: A patriotic movement concerned about national strength would favour it, though the texts say little about armaments.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Their anti-immigrant stance and Biétry's antisemitism treated the French nation as native-born and Christian in character.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The yellows built their doctrine against the Marxist idea of class struggle, calling for cooperation of capital and labour.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Jaunes wanted workers to rise by acquiring property and a share of profits within a hierarchy of firms; equal outcomes is a socialist goal they rejected.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not addressed and no principle clearly decides it.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Not addressed; a nationalist movement of the French empire era would reject it.

civilizational-union.rationale: Not addressed; the emphasis was national, not civilisational.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The program appeals to workers' own interest in property while valuing association and the nation, so the answer is split.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The conclusion roots the individual in family, province and fatherland through association, suggesting community ties come first, though the program also claims rights.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmental ethics postdates the movement; nothing in Biétry's texts bears on the value of nature, so this is neutral.

limit-population.rationale: Nationalist pro-family movement of declining-birthrate France would not favour limiting population; inferred.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Biétry said the Jaunes would not touch the marvellous apparatus of civilisation and wanted to enter the factory as associates.

accelerate-technology.rationale: The Jaunes accepted existing industry but never discussed speeding up technological change at the cost of institutions, which they wanted preserved.

human-enhancement.rationale: Enhancement technology is far outside a 1900s worker-reform movement, and no principle of theirs decides it either way.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Algorithmic rule is anachronistic for this period; the movement's trust in syndicates and chambers of competence does not settle it.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Encryption is anachronistic for a 1900s movement, and its strong-state outlook offsets its liberty talk, so neutral.

restore-past-order.rationale: Jaunes sought progress through property and association yet also reaction; neither frame dominates.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Biétry stressed a concrete programme of practical benefits but also a firm doctrine; split.

direct-action.rationale: Biétry left the Marxists partly over the general strike and the Jaunes opposed political strikes.

means-match-ends.rationale: The sources give no doctrine on whether means must mirror ends, though they chose peaceful association as both method and aim.

return-to-foraging.rationale: The Jaunes explicitly accepted the industrial apparatus of civilisation as theirs to join.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Their model keeps syndicates by trade and corporation with employers and workers each in their roles.

distribute-by-need.rationale: They tied workers' claims to profit shares from capital purchased, which is a form of reward by stake, not by need.

production-for-use.rationale: The Jaunes accepted capitalist firms and profit, wanting workers to share in them.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The program asks for a share of profits and says labour and capital should cooperate; profit is not seen as exploitation.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The Jaunes opposed Marxism and the program attacks class rule by collectivists.

collective-farming.rationale: The program defends property rights and Jaunes organised agricultural syndicates of owners.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Biétry did not hold capitalist war theory; he blamed internationalism and wanted capital-labour harmony in national interest.

taxation-theft.rationale: The movement asked a strong state to secure workers' pensions and mutual aid, so taxation is legitimate; Biétry attacked the swelling budget but not taxation as such.

harm-principle.rationale: A strong-state movement that backed moral order would not limit the state to harm prevention; inferred.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The program gives syndicates unrestricted property rights, so groups hold rights too.

conscription.rationale: A patriotic movement that stressed the army and the nation would accept conscription, which France had; inferred.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The movement tied workers to the fatherland and rejected the rootless "where I do well, there is my country" attitude.

state-as-business.rationale: Biétry fought state-run monopolies yet envisioned a strong state, which is not a customer-citizen model.

positive-liberty.rationale: The program asks for improvements needed for the workers' physical, intellectual and moral development, which echoes the idea, but the framing is not about freedom.

media-academia-power.rationale: Not documented, though Biétry's polemics attacked the press and intellectuals; unclear.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Biétry's antisemitism treated Jews as a distinct race in some of his writing, but a view on genetic ability gaps is not documented.

organic-representation.rationale: The federation aimed to unite workers', farmers' and employers' syndicates into a Party of National Interests and Biétry proposed chambers of competence; representation by trade bodies is central.

total-state.rationale: The state was strong and authoritarian, but Biétry fought state monopolies and collectivism, so the state would not direct all of life.

national-rebirth.rationale: The Jaunes spoke of a programme of national renaissance and Biétry moved from socialism to nationalism.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Not documented; patriotic but focused on domestic order.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: A modern industrial movement with parliamentary politics; feudal oaths play no role.

bound-labor.rationale: The program seeks to free workers into property and association, the opposite of bound labour.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Not addressed; the movement used a rationalist social-reform vocabulary and moral appeal.

universal-morality.rationale: The program appeals to light, justice, truth and progress as its principles, suggesting universal moral claims, but this is inference.

single-common-good.rationale: The yellows held that capital and labour share one national interest and should be united in a Party of National Interests.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Biétry was antisemitic and blamed Jews for socialism; Zionism is not discussed in the sources read.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: The Jaunes texts say nothing on diasporas or return rights, and their nationalism is inward on French workers.

revive-national-language.rationale: No source discusses language revival; French was already the state language in their setting.

workplace-democracy.rationale: They wanted workers as partners with profit shares and joint syndicate agreements, not votes in company management.

school-vouchers.rationale: The program demands liberty of teaching and Biétry filed a bill to separate schools from the state, which is consistent with choice in schooling.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Biétry complained that a swelling state budget crushes the French and called for curbing it.

economic-freedom.rationale: Biétry defended property and association freedoms yet accepted a strong state; the link between economic and political liberty is not argued.

rule-by-example.rationale: The program relies on laws, syndicates and state; moral example of rulers is not a theme.

national-self-determination.rationale: The movement's nationalism affirms the nation as the basic unit, though its texts focus on France.

force-without-un.rationale: Anachronistic; a national-interest movement would not defer to supranational bodies.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Not documented; Biétry defended Christianity against materialism but made no case for faith over reason.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Yellow socialists opposed immigration to protect native workers' jobs, which implies reserving benefits for the native-born.

work-for-welfare.rationale: The Jaunes stressed mutual aid, work and self-reliance through property, so a work expectation is likely, but it is inferred.

class-collaboration.rationale: Cooperation between labour and capital rather than class conflict is the core idea of yellow socialism; the federation's stated aim was to cement the accord of capital and labour.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Biétry said they would not tear down the inherited machinery of civilisation.

dominated-front.rationale: A front of dominated countries against the West belongs to later anticolonial politics and has no counterpart in Jaune writings.

workers-nation.rationale: Biétry argued that internationalism dupes French workers and that workers should be bound to the nation.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The Jaunes had a women's league in support, but I found no programme for gender roles; a conservative movement of the time would accept distinct roles.

ban-interest.rationale: Biétry's antisemitic rhetoric attacked Jewish finance but he promoted capital participation, so an interest ban is not his programme.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Biétry was antisemitic but no source documents segregation by race law; unknown.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The movement saw the state as a national arbiter of capital and labour, not a class tool.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Anachronistic; no basis in sources for a position.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Their nationalism and opposition to immigration point to expecting newcomers to adopt the national culture, though no text states it.

elite-replacement.rationale: The Jaunes held a conspiracy view about Jews and socialism, but not a modern replacement theory; adherents would not state it.

proportional-representation.rationale: Biétry complained that deputies represent unequal numbers of voters, but no proportional system is proposed in what I read.

national-mission.rationale: Not addressed; a defensive nationalism more than a missionary one.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Anachronistic; a conservative, nationalist movement would reject the claim.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Biétry attacked an omnipotent, absent parliament and state socialism's functionaries and ran against the political class as a worker-deputy.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenic policy is not discussed in the Jaune sources I read, so no position can be documented.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: A patriotic, order-minded movement would resist this; anachronistic.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The Jaunes wanted the state to uphold pensions, assistance and conciliation between classes, and described a strong state above syndicates.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Biétry's racial antisemitism may suggest so, but no source documents it, so no firm view.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The program claims equal civic rights for workers yet Biétry's antisemitism denied it to Jews; adherents split.

socialism-one-country.rationale: The statement is Marxist and not framed in Jaune doctrine, which opposed international socialism.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: A French nationalist movement of the colonial era would not accept this frame; inferred.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: The program wants liberty of conscience and a uniform national citizenry; not documented on civil codes.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The program defends absolute liberty of conscience.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: The question comes from South Asian politics and has no bearing on a French labour movement.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Biétry fought anticlericalism in schools yet demanded freedom of teaching; adherents split on religious instruction in state schools.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: The proposition belongs to Marxist-Leninist debates and has no link to Jaune doctrine.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Biétry sat in parliament and addressed voters but the movement favoured a strong authoritarian state; split.

trade-surplus.rationale: Not addressed; some concern for exports in Biétry's speech, but no trade doctrine.

population-transfer.rationale: Biétry's antisemitism may suggest it but no source documents expulsions, so no firm stance.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The movement rejected revolutionary violence but not state coercion; a strict nonaggression principle is foreign to it.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: The Jaunes sought harmony of capital and labour but also valued commerce and competition resting on strong syndicates.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: A strong-state, anti-Marxist movement would likely accept outlawing revolutionary parties; inferred.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Not addressed; the program talks of freeing workers from the anonymous state master, which resembles it, but they would not have put it so.

separated-powers.rationale: Biétry objected to an omnipotent parliament and proposed chambers of competence as a check, which is a division of power.

vanguard-party.rationale: The Jaunes rejected Marxism, and Biétry left Marxist party politics for non-political syndicalism.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The program puts workers' improvement first but through cooperation with employers; priority to the poor is not stated.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Spreading ownership to workers is central, though housing is not discussed.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: The program opposes political strikes and strikes not shown necessary by employer intransigence; the movement began as non-strikers' unions.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Not argued; they blamed wage-system anarchy and collectivism.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The movement opposed immigration and put national unity at the centre, which implies this view.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Not in the program; a movement for strong order and competence would reject it.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Not documented; strong-state tendencies versus a stated absolute liberty of conscience.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price controls on foods are not addressed; the Jaunes favoured agreed wages and hours rather than state price-fixing, leaving a neutral stance.

party-controls-media.rationale: Biétry published his own press and defended liberties of association and teaching, so state control of media is not his programme.

party-commands-army.rationale: They stressed the national army and fatherland, not a party command.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Opposition to immigration suggests restrictive naturalisation, but no source documents it.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: No source states what deputies should be paid; Biétry himself sat as a paid deputy without comment on it.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Not addressed; Biétry sat as non-affiliated deputy.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The Jaunes attacked internationalism and centred national unity.

head-commands-forces.rationale: A strong authoritarian state implies executive command; inferred.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is a question internal to churches and the Jaunes took no view beyond liberty of conscience.

clerical-rule.rationale: The movement wanted liberty of conscience and syndicates, not clerical rule.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Biétry attacked the internationalist abandonment of the tricolour; defeat of one's own government is opposed.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Not addressed; liberty of teaching and conscience in the program, but moralism in the movement.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Presidential term rules are not discussed in the sources; Biétry's complaints concern parliament's powers, not tenure.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall of officials is not in the Jaune program or Biétry's speeches I read, so neutral.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Their nationalism favours a strong France, but nothing in the sources addresses alliances or troop deployments.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: The movement wanted wider ownership but did not seek abolition of private lettings; inferred.

people-in-arms.rationale: Patriotic nationalists favoured the army; no basis for armed citizenry.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Jaunes organised agricultural syndicates besides industrial ones but no moral preference for rural life is documented.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: A nationalist movement would likely approve; not documented.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Biétry was a worker-polemicist who spoke against intellectuals and politicians; inferred.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Nationalist and antisemitic; they would not hold all cultures equal.

death-penalty.rationale: Not documented; a law-and-order nationalist movement of 1900 would back it.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: The program asks for civic and professional education and a conservative moral outlook is typical of the movement, so adherents would reject sex education.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Anachronistic; Jaunes favoured liberty of teaching without a doctrine on evolution.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Anachronistic; a conservative, moralist movement would back restrictions.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The movement's concern for native-born workers suggests descent over birth-on-territory; inferred.

minority-language-support.rationale: Nationalist unity of France is central; inferred.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Absolute liberty of conscience is in the program, but exemptions from general laws are not addressed.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Not addressed; their communitarian and patriotic outlook suggests not.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Anachronistic; a property-defending movement would reject debt cancellation.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Decolonisation questions are absent from the Jaunes sources; the movement itself wanted ownership spread within the existing order.

constituent-assembly.rationale: No Jaune text calls for rewriting the constitution; Biétry argued for adding chambers of competence within the republic.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Strong-state leanings suggest openness but no text addresses it.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: A national-first movement concerned with French workers and against internationalism would not accept a duty of global aid.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Anachronistic; patriotic movement favouring national strength.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Nothing in the sources addresses how the head of state is chosen.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Central banking policy is not discussed in the sources read; the movement was concerned with the wage system, not monetary institutions.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Nationalist movement; inferred and not documented.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Biétry defended property as a right without restriction, even if its spread serves national good.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Anachronistic; the Soviet Union did not yet exist; they would still call collectivism harmful.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental risk regulation did not exist as an issue in the period and no Jaune principle decides it.

collective-defense.rationale: Not documented; patriotic movement likely backs alliances for national defence.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: The sources do not discuss annexation; a French nationalist might sympathise with lost Alsace-Lorraine, but this is not documented.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Biétry fought anticlericalism and the program demands liberty of conscience and teaching.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Whether the head of state stands above party is not addressed; the Jaunes wanted a Party of National Interests but also a strong state above groups.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: The movement made national unity central, so force to preserve it is plausible; inferred.

region-keeps-system.rationale: A high-autonomy region sits badly with the insistence on national unity under one tricolour that Biétry voiced.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Biétry was a republican, not a divine-right monarchist.

flat-income-tax.rationale: No tax-rate doctrine appears in the Jaune program, which complained of the budget's size rather than its structure.

character-from-environment.rationale: Not addressed; their approach to workers' uplift stresses education and conditions, which hints at environment, but the Jaunes did not argue it.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Strong state but Biétry himself complained of unrestrained parliamentary power and sought chambers of competence as a check.

space-expansion.rationale: Space expansion is far outside the period, and no Jaune principle bears on it.

mixed-constitution.rationale: The chambers of competence alongside parliament resemble a mixed arrangement; inferred from the speech.

leader-cult.rationale: Biétry was a charismatic leader but no source documents a leader cult.

equal-parenting.rationale: Child custody presumptions are anachronistic and not discussed in the sources.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Marxist formula; the Jaunes deny class struggle altogether.

land-redistribution.rationale: Property rights are central and the program defends property without restriction.

refugee-return.rationale: Refugee return rights are not addressed in the Jaune sources and do not follow from their principles.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Claims over territory abroad are not discussed in the Jaune sources; their nationalism is aimed at French workers' unity.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The program states absolute liberty of conscience and Biétry affirmed everyone's right to practise their forefathers' religion.

common-currency.rationale: Currency union is anachronistic; a movement stressing national unity and sovereignty would not welcome sharing money with others.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: The movement centred the French nation; pan-ethnic union unmentioned.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Separate self-governing minority institutions cut against Biétry's unitary French nationalism, so adherents would disagree.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: The movement saw Jews as an alien conspiratorial minority, so it would not endorse this; inferred.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Biétry attacked the materialist conception of history as destroying ideals, religions and the fatherland.

ban-cartels.rationale: The Jaunes wanted employer and worker syndicates organised by trade, which are a kind of cartel of interests.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailouts of failing firms are not discussed; the movement was pro-property but also wanted employer-worker cooperation, so no clear line.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Judicial review is not discussed; Biétry wanted checks on parliament, not freedom for majorities, yet no view on courts.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Quotas for women in public bodies are anachronistic and clash with a conservative outlook on gender roles.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Biétry complained of industries unable to export, so closed blocs are unlikely, but nationalism cuts the other way.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Binding standards in trade deals are anachronistic; a nationalist movement would back protection of workers but through national means.

moral-incentives.rationale: The Jaunes tied workers to the system through share ownership and profit, which are material incentives.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The Jaunes opposed revolution and political strike.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Republican in name but part of a movement mixed with the reactionary right; not documented.

history-own-civilization.rationale: National patriotism suggests it; not documented.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: French nationalism of the colonial era; inferred and undocumented.

patriotic-education.rationale: The program demands civic and professional education for all workers and Biétry made love of the fatherland central.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: The issue is anachronistic, but a movement that rejected group-based claims in favour of national unity would back ending preferences.

public-money-creation.rationale: Money creation is not discussed in the sources; the Jaunes did not propose monetary reform.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The Jaunes held that capitalism could be reformed by profit sharing and worker shareholding and rejected a collapse theory.

former-empire-influence.rationale: French cultural and political influence in former imperial regions is not discussed in the sources read.

delink-world-market.rationale: Not addressed; they wanted industries able to export.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Leninist theory that Jaunes reject, believing workers share interest with their own nation.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The movement favoured property rights without restriction but was not libertarian.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The Jaunes listed freedoms of association, teaching and conscience and property rights, but did not discuss entrenching them against majorities.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Colonial treaty questions are not touched by the Jaune sources.

elective-rulers.rationale: Biétry accepted republican politics and sat as elected deputy.

minority-veto.rationale: A veto for dissenting members would make syndicate agreements and national decisions unworkable; a unitary strong-state movement rejects it.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Resistance to rulers is not discussed; the Jaunes opposed revolution but also criticised an omnipotent parliament.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Biétry criticised an omnipotent parliament and proposed chambers of competence for economic laws.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal welfare is not addressed in the Jaune sources and is anachronistic for the period.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal use is not addressed in the sources read; no principle of the movement decides it.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Patriotic cooperation between classes and encouragement of charity in the program fit it, though the wording is not theirs.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Biétry entered parliament and built a federation and party; the program calls for civic education.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Critical theory of mass culture is not part of the Jaune outlook, and nothing in the sources addresses media culture.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: The Gramscian idea of cultural hegemony is foreign to the Jaunes, who denied there were opposed classes to dominate each other.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Not addressed; they reject Marxist exploitation analysis.

native-born-offices.rationale: Anti-immigrant nationalism suggests it; not documented.

party-own-road.rationale: The question concerns national roads within the Marxist movement, which the Jaunes opposed, so there is no Jaune position.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Development aid is not an issue in the sources; the movement was concerned with French workers.

return-lost-territory.rationale: French nationalism; Alsace-Lorraine revanchism is typical of the period but not documented here.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Not addressed; colonial-era nationalism would reject.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Anachronistic; they were precursors to some on the far right.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The comparison of fascism and communism postdates the movement, which opposed Marxism but also later had links to far-right currents.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: American Civil War history is not touched by the Jaune sources.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Monument disputes are anachronistic, but a movement committed to national tradition and patriotism would favour keeping them.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: The issue is anachronistic and nothing in the sources decides it.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: The issue is anachronistic and nothing in the sources decides it.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: National organicism points to home-grown forms; inferred.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Not documented; patriotic army-respecting movement but also parliamentary.

paid-care-work.rationale: Wages for domestic work are anachronistic and clash with the family-centred conservatism of the period.

filial-duty.rationale: The conclusion rests society on the individual, family, province and fatherland, suggesting family obligations, though filial duty is not stated.

office-by-exam.rationale: Biétry offered chambers of competence, but no civil-service doctrine.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Blocking foreign buyers of strategic firms fits their nationalism, but it is not documented in the Jaune sources.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Easier divorce is anachronistic and clashes with the movement's family-centred conservatism.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Binding mandates and instant recall belong to council-democracy ideas the Jaunes rejected, though they did not discuss them.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: The program calls for mutual aid and workers' pensions guaranteed through organisations, not private individual accounts.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The program defends property rights and spread of ownership.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Biétry criticised parliament's spending yet did not deny its budget role; inferred.

single-official-language.rationale: A sole national language fits the French nationalism of the Jaunes but is not stated in their texts.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Barring foreign landowners fits their nationalism and hostility to outsiders, but the sources do not state it.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Disparate-impact doctrine is anachronistic and clashes with the movement's rejection of group-based claims.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Consumerism critique is not discussed; the Jaunes wanted workers to acquire property and a share in profits.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Covert support to foreign insurgents is not discussed in the sources read.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Bloc discipline is a Cold War question and does not touch the Jaunes.

corporate-influence.rationale: The movement wanted capital-labour partnership, not anti-corporate measures, and distrusted state officials; no stance.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Limits on foreign funding of NGOs and media fit their sovereignty-minded nationalism, but are not documented.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Pro-family nationalism would favour it over immigration; inferred.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local limits on property purchases are not discussed, and the movement's property-first outlook cuts against them too.

job-guarantee.rationale: The movement opposed state functionaries and collectivism; a state job guarantee runs against it.

democratic-peace.rationale: Democratic peace theory postdates the movement and is not discussed in its sources.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: A law-and-order nationalist movement under a strong state.

non-intervention.rationale: Non-intervention as an absolute rule is not discussed in the sources; nationalism does not decide it.

industrial-unions.rationale: The Jaunes organised by corporation, region and trade, mixing employers and workers in the same trade bodies, rather than industry-wide worker unions.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Biétry's book blames Jews for socialism and collectivism; later the FNJF program added antisemitism.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Ending state-recognised marriage is irreconcilable with the family-centred conservatism of the movement.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Freedom-of-information rights are not discussed in the Jaune sources.

local-production.rationale: Local production is not discussed; Biétry lamented industries unable to export, which cuts against localism.

informal-organisation.rationale: They built a national federation of syndicates, a party and a press.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The movement's nationalism and attack on internationalism implies national law would come first, though this is not stated directly.

religious-nation.rationale: Biétry stressed liberty of conscience but treated Christianity as French heritage.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Not applicable to France and its nationalism.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Regions keeping their own revenue cuts against the insistence on national unity, though fiscal issues are not discussed.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Biétry's property doctrine goes further than personal possessions to productive ownership, but accepts the point.

defeat-communism.rationale: The yellow movement was built against Marxism, fought collectivism and called it a danger.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Service delivery models are not addressed; the program opposed state functionaries but backed mutual and charitable providers.

religion-illusion.rationale: Biétry criticised the Marxist claim that religion reflects social conditions and defended Christianity against materialism.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: They kept the industrial apparatus and wanted workers to become shareholders in it.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Not addressed; a conservative movement would reject.

socialized-care.rationale: Public housework and childcare would conflict with the family-centred conservatism of the movement.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Purging loanwords is not discussed in the Jaune sources.

treaties-binding.rationale: Treaties between governments and internal nations are not discussed in the sources.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Property held in common conflicts with their individual property emphasis.

majority-settlement.rationale: Settlement policy in minority regions is not discussed in the sources read.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Yellow socialism was proposed as a third way between Marxist red socialism and unreformed capitalism, though it was not hostile to capitalism.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Historical or religious claims to land are not discussed in the Jaune sources.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Anachronistic, as the events occurred after the movement ended.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Anachronistic; French law did not criminalise it after 1791; not discussed.

suppress-opposition.rationale: A strong authoritarian state is described, but no source records Biétry calling for suppression of opposition; he sat in parliament as an independent.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Absolute liberty of conscience in the program.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: This is an Islamic legal question with no bearing on a French labour movement.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: The movement opposed revolution and sought liberty of conscience.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The movement used syndicates and a strong state rather than direct popular participation.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Class conflict is rejected and the framework is anachronistic.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Legal gender identity is anachronistic and would be rejected by a conservative movement of the period.

assisted-dying.rationale: Assisted dying is anachronistic; the conservative, Christian-friendly outlook of the movement points against it.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Yellow socialism was a non-Marxist socialism mixing labour reform with nationalism, drawing both left and right support.

alienated-labor.rationale: Marxist analysis; the Jaunes instead answered the wage system with share ownership.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Islam is not discussed in the sources read, so no position is documented.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Not documented; Biétry sat in a republican parliament.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Biétry defended liberty of conscience and opposed anticlerical measures, but no view on dress.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Nondisclosure agreements are anachronistic and not covered by any Jaune source.

social-market-economy.rationale: They proposed a market economy with employer-worker syndicates, profit sharing and mutual aid and pensions, between laissez-faire and collectivism.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Patriotic nationalists and attached to national strength.

rich-first.rationale: Letting some grow rich first is a development slogan with no counterpart in Jaune writings.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Bloc membership is not discussed in the Jaune sources.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Biétry was a republican deputy and the Jaunes claimed no dynasty, so hereditary succession of leaders is not part of the doctrine.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Their mutual aid ideas suggest sympathy, but nothing on credit.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: IMF austerity conditions are anachronistic and nothing in the sources decides it.

property-franchise.rationale: Biétry aimed at spreading property to workers and spoke as an elected republican deputy.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Ecofeminist theory is anachronistic and would not be accepted by the movement.

reification.rationale: Reification is a Marxist-Lukacsian theory of capitalism, whereas the Jaunes opposed Marxism and rejected its analysis.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: A property-defending movement that ran its own papers rejects the claim.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Rule through announced laws is implicit in a republic where Biétry sat as deputy, though not stated in the Jaune texts.

racial-franchise.rationale: Antisemitic but no source documents exclusion of Jews from the vote.

online-participation.rationale: Internet participation is anachronistic and no principle decides it.

open-government-data.rationale: Open data is anachronistic and not covered by any source.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Interfaith marriage law is not discussed; the program defends liberty of conscience, though antisemitism may have supported such a view.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Biétry's antisemitism praised Drumont; boycotts are not documented but typical of the milieu.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Anachronistic; they proposed chambers of competence of different design.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: The Jaunes defended freedom to practise one's inherited religion and did not discuss reform of doctrine.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The Jaunes opposed state collectivism but also called for workers' accession to capital, which implicitly worries about concentration; the doctrine is not worded that way.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: The issue is anachronistic, and the conservative outlook of the movement would reject it.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Biétry criticised atheist materialism and opposed anticlericalism and demanded absolute liberty of conscience.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: A movement upholding order and a strong state would reject abolishing police and prisons.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Consociational power-sharing is not discussed and does not follow from their principles.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The program encourages private charity initiatives and mutual aid and attacks state collectivism.

term-limits.rationale: Term limits for politicians are not discussed in the Jaune sources.

vote-delegation.rationale: Liquid delegation of votes is anachronistic and outside the sources.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Existential risk is anachronistic and not addressed by any source.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Women's ordination is anachronistic, and a Christian-friendly conservative movement would not support it.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Marital authority is not discussed in the sources read, though the Jaunes had a women's league in support of their cause.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: The movement opposed immigration and internationalism.

rent-control.rationale: Rent caps are not discussed; the movement wanted to spread ownership rather than regulate tenancy.

abolish-ip.rationale: The program asserts property rights without restriction for syndicates and individuals, which suggests opposing abolition of patents and copyrights.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Uniformed youth movements are not discussed in the sources, though the federation did stress civic education.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Nuclear weapons are anachronistic and no Jaune principle decides it.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Foreign bases are not discussed in the sources read.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Genocide recognition is anachronistic and not addressed in the Jaune sources.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The program seeks worker property and profit shares, which accepts returns on capital, yet Biétry attacked finance and idle capital; inferred as split.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: A patriotic movement hostile to internationalism and loyal to national defence is inferred to reject any bar on lethal defence; the sources do not address it directly.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Biétry's movement was patriotic and moved toward nationalism, so it is inferred to see the French nation as continuous, though the sources do not state this.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: The 1900s movement never addressed this, and its conservative outlook suggests rejection by inference; anachronistic.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Anachronistic; a conservative workers' movement is inferred to take women as a shared category, not a plural one.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: The movement was patriotic but opposed clericalism and made liberty of conscience part of its program, so sacred veneration is inferred as split.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Yellow socialism stressed class cooperation and practical gains for workers, so a cosmic good-versus-evil view of politics is inferred to be rejected.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: As a nationalist movement hostile to immigration it is inferred to want the people gathered in the nation, not scattered; the sources do not address diaspora.

culture-before-state.rationale: Its strong national state and political action through syndicates imply state and economic order take priority over cultural renewal; inferred.

god-not-male.rationale: Anachronistic; a conservative, patriotic movement is inferred to keep traditional religious language.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Anachronistic; the movement's conservative outlook is inferred to treat religious texts as authoritative as they stand.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: The movement opposed immigration and, increasingly, targeted Jews in business and finance, which implies a wish for the national majority to hold economic life.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Regional boundaries were not a concern of the program or Biétry's speeches; no position can be inferred.

independent-unions.rationale: The Jaunes kept their syndicates apart from political parties, but their corporatist programme looked to a strong authoritarian state, so independence from the state is not clearly held; this is an inference.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The Jaunes rejected class struggle and sought workers' property and profit shares within a cooperating-classes order under a strong state.

local-essentials-public.rationale: The program opposes state collectivism but backs a strong state and social assistance; no source addresses local services.

second-chamber.rationale: Biétry attacked parliament but the sources give no view on a second chamber.

municipal-property.rationale: The movement wanted workers to own shares in firms and rejected collective ownership by community or state.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Inferred from its strong national state and corporatist organisation; local assembly sovereignty is not in the program.

family-wage.rationale: Inferred from its pro-family patriotism and pensions and assistance demands; no wage statement was found.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from its strong-state nationalism.

online-anonymity.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from its strong-state nationalism.

person-over-state.rationale: The program stresses liberty of conscience yet puts the nation and a strong state first; adherents' view is inferred.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Biétry opposed anticlericalism and defended liberty of conscience, which suggests acceptance of the spiritual; inferred.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Inferred from its strong centralised national state; regional self-government is not discussed.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Its nationalism was framed around nation and class, with antisemitic passages, but it did not organise by race groups; contested reading.

racial-pride.rationale: Its patriotic nationalism implies pride in national ancestry; the sources do not use the term race.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Patriotic and anti-internationalist but no stated doctrine on wars of aggression.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Biétry's program is built on the French state and patriotism and does not define the nation by language; a language-based nation spanning borders is inferred to sit poorly with it.

communal-electorates.rationale: The movement wanted one strong national state and workers organised by trade, not by religion; separate religious electorates are inferred to be foreign to it.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: The Jaunes were hostile to internationalism and foreign influence, but the sources show no claim of a foreign plot to partition France, so this is left neutral.

free-public-college.rationale: The program does not address tuition; Biétry's school-bill stance concerned freedom of schooling, so no position on free college can be inferred.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Environmental taxes are anachronistic; the movement favoured property-owning workers and a strong state without a stated view on pricing pollution.

future-generations.rationale: A patriotic, family- and property-oriented movement would accept a duty to hand on the homeland intact; inferred from its nationalism, not stated.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Yellow socialism was socially conservative and nationalist, so giving women's distinct values extra weight in public life is inferred to be foreign to it.

arms-reduction.rationale: As a patriotic movement under a strong national state, it is inferred to have favoured keeping national defence strong, not cutting arms.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Nationalist, anti-parliament and hostile to internationalism, the Jaunes are inferred to have accepted confidential state diplomacy; the sources do not discuss it.

capital-controls.rationale: A strong-state corporatism hostile to international finance and aiming at national workers' property is inferred to accept state limits on capital flows.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred from the strong national state the Jaunes wanted and their patriotism, though the sources do not discuss private arms.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Biétry's Jaunes were patriotic and hostile to internationalism and antimilitarism, opposing the red socialist call for soldiers' refusal.

collective-bargaining.rationale: The Jaunes wanted wages and conditions set by joint syndicates cooperating with employers, which is close to collective negotiation, though they rejected class-struggle unionism and wanted company-level syndicates.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: The program backed profit sharing and pensions rather than state tax top-ups, and does not address tax credits.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: The program does not address public borrowing; a strong state and anti-collectivism give no clear direction.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Inferred from their nationalism and focus on French workers and national industry, which was hostile to internationalism.

smash-state-machine.rationale: They rejected class struggle and revolution, and wanted a strong national state, so smashing it is not their position; they also attacked parliament, so inferred.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Propriétarisme rejected a fixed collectivist blueprint and wanted workers to gain property through syndicates and profit sharing, but they still sought a national framework.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Inferred from the focus on workers' property in firms; the sources do not mention nature.

sacred-nation.rationale: The Jaunes were patriotic and nationalist and valued the nation as a lasting community, though the sources do not call it sacred.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Not addressed in the program; student loans did not exist as a political issue in that period.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Inferred from their strong national state and anti-Marxist unity, which did not frame regions as colonies.

shared-human-nature.rationale: The sources do not address human nature; the Jaunes' antisemitism and exclusion of immigrants cuts against universal dignity, while liberty of conscience cuts for it.

public-service-media.rationale: Biétry's Jaunes attacked the parliamentary system and favoured strong national direction, so state-funded media free of control is not supported; inferred.

religions-one-truth.rationale: The Jaunes defended liberty of conscience and opposed anticlericalism but never taught that all religions share one truth; inferred.

farm-price-support.rationale: A patriotic corporatism that protects producers and rejects free markets and state collectivism both would plausibly back supports for farmers; inferred.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Inferred from the strongly patriotic, strong-state outlook; the question is anachronistic for 1902-1912.

workers-own-party.rationale: Biétry rejected class-based socialist party politics, yet he sat as a deputy and founded a party of his own movement, so the stance on a separate workers' party is mixed; this is an inference.

ban-fgm.rationale: The Jaunes never addressed it and nothing can be inferred.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Their propertyism wanted workers to own property, and French inheritance law was equal among children; inferred.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Inferred from nationalism in a centralised French state that treated French as the national language.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Propertyism favours protecting property but the strong state favours regulation; the sources are silent.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: A strong centralised nation-state leaves no place for customary chiefs; inferred.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Inferred from their emphasis on production, property and liberty of owners; the question is anachronistic.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred from their law-and-order, strong-state nationalism.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: They were hostile to immigration, so a language requirement is inferred to be welcome.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Yellow unions were founded partly to protect workers who refused to strike or join red syndicates, so they are inferred to oppose compelled membership.

voter-id.rationale: Inferred from its patriotic, nationalist and anti-immigrant stance, which favours limiting the franchise to proven citizens.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The program does not discuss legal status of religious interpretations; split between Catholic sympathisers and secular nationalists.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Biétry was a nationalist hostile to parliamentary politics yet ran for election himself, so adherents are split on a purely procedural test.

premarital-sex.rationale: Inferred from its patriotic, family-centred and conservative social outlook.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred from its strong national state and order-focused outlook; the topic is anachronistic.

negative-income-tax.rationale: The program sought worker property and profit-sharing within firms through syndicates, not a state cash-transfer replacing welfare.

women-suffrage.rationale: The program does not address women's suffrage; adherents' views are not documented.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Inferred from its conservative, anti-Marxist outlook, which did not blame religion for social ills.

race-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from its increasingly antisemitic and nationalist outlook, which treated groups as having inherent traits.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred from its conservative social views; no gender policy appears in its program.

homestead-ownership.rationale: The program deals with how workers gain property through savings and profit sharing, and says nothing about first claims to unowned resources, so this is not inferable either way.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred from the movement's patriotism and hostility to internationalism, which suggests it would distrust courts above the nation.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: The program guarantees liberty of conscience and opposes anticlericalism but states no doctrine of scripture; a literal-inerrancy position is not inferable.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred from a nationalist, corporatist movement that showed no concern for gender-equality guarantees in group self-rule.

defend-planned-state.rationale: The Jaunes rejected state collectivism and Marxism and wanted workers to gain private property and profit shares, so a state-owned planned economy was not something to defend.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred from its critique of parliament and its wish for a strong national state; no source discusses indirect council selection.

national-church-status.rationale: The movement opposed anticlericalism but its program stresses liberty of conscience for all; inferred that it did not seek legal precedence for one church.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Inferred from its strong unitary national state and patriotism, which leave little room for ethnic territorial autonomy.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred from a nationalist outlook that treats the fate of territory as a matter for the national state, not local votes.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Inferred from its patriotic respect for established national states and borders; no source addresses colonial borders.

simple-living.rationale: Its goal was to give workers property and a share of prosperity, which is not an ideal of limited needs; inferred from the program.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Hostile to immigration, but the movement had no concept of indigenous homelands, so the statement does not map onto its positions.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred from a patriotic movement in a France where conscription applied to men only; no source mentions women in the draft.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: The Jaunes were patriotic and tied workers' welfare to a strong French nation.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Not addressed; inferred only as a nationalist movement, with no sources on drug policy, which is anachronistic.

close-ties-china.rationale: Inferred from hostility to internationalism; the sources do not discuss China, and this is anachronistic.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Inferred from the strand's nationalism; kin minorities abroad are not discussed in the sources.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on private property for workers, not common ownership.

self-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the programme of workers owning property and shares of their firms.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Not addressed; the programme stressed profit-sharing and mutual aid through syndicates.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Inferred: Biétry wanted workers' syndicates cooperating with employers under a strong state, using groups rather than bypassing them.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Inferred from hostility to financial capital and favouring small property; not directly discussed.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Inferred from patriotic, anti-internationalist conservatism combined with modern industry.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Not addressed; adherents' views are not recorded.

national-resource-control.rationale: Inferred from patriotism and wanting the French economy kept under national control.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Inferred from the Jaunes' view that property and profit shares are earned by labour and cooperation.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from hostility to international finance.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Inferred from the strand's strong state and order, and no natural-law tradition in the sources.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Inferred from the aim of workers sharing in industry through profit and property, not shorter work through automation.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Inferred from the claim that workers deserve a share of profits as producers of wealth.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: The Jaunes joined patriotism with a workers' movement as the programme's core claim, against internationalist red socialism.

material-over-identity.rationale: Inferred from the focus on workers' property and profit shares over cultural questions.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: The movement rejected class struggle and state collectivism and was hostile to communist parties.

missingStatements.text: Workers should receive a share of their company's profits and be encouraged to hold shares in it.
missingStatements.rationale: The Jaunes program and Biétry's slogan demand participation of labour in the profits of capital, starting from workers buying a share of the firm.

notes: Evidence is thin outside the 1904 program, so most answers rest on inference from its nationalism, property doctrine and anti-collectivism; many questions are anachronistic. Biétry's own claims about Jews and about Marxism are recorded as documented positions, not endorsed. Sources s1 passages came from the archive.org text, which I searched by keyword rather than reading end to end.
